title: Stratified microburst sentinel for CI performance regression detection
creator: Marco Li
summary: Introduce a lightweight CI prober that executes stratified microburst workloads to detect regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency without adding significant CI time.
description: Background: Current CI regression gates rely on full long-running harnesses or coarse baseline comparisons which either increase CI latency or miss short-lived performance regressions that manifest as bursts in token throughput or p95 tail shifts. Objective: build a stratified microburst sentinel that runs short, deterministic microbursts across representative slices (sequence lengths, batch sizes, model variants) and computes bootstrap confidence bands for tokens/sec and p95. The sentinel must be cheap (<6 minutes total), reproducible in PR CI, produce a small artifact with time-series and slice-level metrics, and emit a probabilistic regression score that can be used as a gating signal (block/soft-fail/annotate).
acceptance_criteria: A prober job that runs in CI under 6 minutes on our standard test runner image
Slices defined: short (<=64), medium (65-512), long (>512) sequence groups and batch sizes [1,4,8] — each slice executes 3 microbursts of 30-90 steps depending on seq len
Computed metrics: tokens_per_sec (mean, median), p95 latency with bootstrap 95% CI per slice
Regression score: returns a single probabilistic score (0..1) where >0.975 triggers block, 0.90-0.975 triggers soft-fail, <0.90 annotates. Configurable thresholds per project
Artifacts: compressed JSON timeseries + slice summary uploaded to CI artifacts and linked in PR comment; dashboard link generated
False-positive rate when testing stable baseline must be <2% across 30 runs
Integration: PR gate implemented in CI workflow with a toggle (off by default) and a rollout plan to opt-in projects
technical_notes: Use deterministic sampling seeds and repeatable input prompts to reduce variance
Microburst composition: warm KV cache with a short priming sequence, then measure steady-state token production for N steps
Use Bayesian bootstrap to estimate p95 uncertainty; prefer percentile-of-blocks over single-run percentiles for stability
Instrument token counters and wall-clock timers at the runtime boundary to avoid jitter from SDK/client code
Provide a lightweight Python harness that uses existing load-gen proto but with strict time budget and early-exit heuristics
Artifacts schema: flat JSON with top-level meta, slices (array of strings), and metrics (array of strings) — keep size <200KB
test_plan: Step 1: Local dev harness - run on dev workstation with same runner image; verify determinism across 5 runs
Step 2: CI stage - add a dedicated job in .github/workflows/ci-perf-sentinel.yaml; test duration and artifact upload
Step 3: Canary - enable sentinel on 'internal-sdk' repo with soft-fail threshold for two weeks; monitor false positives
Step 4: Gate rollout - after 2 weeks and FP <2%, enable blocking for newly onboarded repos behind a feature flag
Step 5: Longitudinal validation - schedule daily sentinel runs against a stable baseline for 2 weeks to validate sensitivity and tune slice weights
updates: 2026-03-01: Initial ticket created. Design spike planned to evaluate bootstrap vs. block aggregation methods.
2026-03-04: Spike results: bootstrap CI reduces run-to-run variance by ~35% compared to naive p95. Decided to use Bayesian bootstrap with 500 resamples.
2026-03-07: Prototype harness implemented (branch: perf/sentinel-microburst). Basic slice runner and artifact writer completed. Local runs stable.
2026-03-09: CI job added to PR for prototype. Observed noise when host CPU contention >40% — added CPU pinning recommendations and early-exit if system is noisy.
2026-03-12: Integration PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4382. Awaiting infra review from @Jordan Reyes. Next: dashboard panel and Slack alerting path.
